issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s agricultural tenancy interest cannot be transferred through a testamentary bequest as a means of obtaining tenancy rights.
material_facts: A tenant applied for occupancy rights in agricultural land under the governing land-reform scheme.
While the application was pending, the tenant made a will bequeathing his tenancy rights; a later claimant asserted rights through a further will made by the first beneficiary.
The tenant’s wife and children were awarded occupancy rights by the Land Tribunal, and the appellate authority and High Court left that decision undisturbed.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that a testamentary disposition of the tenancy interest amounts to an assignment prohibited by Section 21 of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961. On the tenant’s death, the tenancy continues under Section 24 for heirs determined under personal law, subject to Section 21; a will cannot confer the tenancy interest on a legatee as a testamentary transfer. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 21 and 24 of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961 must be read together: Section 21 prohibits assignment of an interest in the tenanted land, subject to its specified family and heir exceptions, while Section 24 continues the tenancy after the tenant’s death on the same terms for the heirs. The relevant heirs are determined by personal law but remain subject to Section 21. A devise under a will is an assignment for this purpose because it deals with and disposes of the tenancy interest, and allowing it would permit strangers to enter the land. The Court regarded Timmakka Kom Venkanna Naik v. The Land Tribunal as the better view and declined to follow the broader statements in Shivanna v. Rachiah and Dhareppa v. State of Karnataka. Angurbala Mullick v. Debabrata Mullick did not assist the appellant because the issue was whether the devise was barred, not whether the word “heir” could have a broad meaning.

predicates.occupancy_rights_proceeding: The proceeding sought recognition of occupancy rights arising from an agricultural tenancy.
predicates.will_based_tenancy_claim: A claimant relied on a tenant’s will to claim the tenant’s tenancy interest.
predicates.testamentary_claim_cannot_transfer_tenan: A testamentary claim does not transfer the tenant’s tenancy rights.

issues.definition: When an occupancy-rights proceeding concerns an agricultural tenancy and a claimant relies on a tenant’s will to claim the tenancy interest, the testamentary claim cannot transfer those rights.
